pages.text: Rafi swims to a coral reef. The reef is colorful and busy, like an underwater neighborhood full of life.
Coral reefs are built by tiny animals called coral polyps. Many polyps together make hard coral shapes.
The reef lives in shallow water where sunlight can reach. Sunlight helps the reef stay strong and colorful.
Small fish hide in coral branches. The reef gives them shelter from bigger animals that might chase them.
Crabs, sea stars, and snails crawl along the reef. Many animals share the reef as a home.
Rafi learns: coral is not a plant and not a rock. Coral is made by tiny animals working together.
Dirty water can hurt reefs. Clean water helps coral and fish stay healthy and safe.
Rafi watches bright colors: pink coral, yellow fish, blue water. The reef looks like a soft rainbow.
Rafi swims slowly and carefully so he does not bump the coral. Reefs can break if we are rough.
Rafi says goodbye to the reef neighborhood. He remembers: tiny coral animals build big homes for many.
